summary: Configured a persistent firewalld firewall on node1 (RHEL 7): SSH is allowed from any source (default public zone), TCP/9000 is allowed only from node2 (10.100.190.11, via a dedicated source-based firewalld zone "node2-9000") and rejected from node3 and everywhere else (reject rich-rule in the public zone). All three managed nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol, with boot-identity change and full service/rule recovery confirmed on each before moving to the next.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (RHEL 7.9, firewalld active) and confirmed ssh already allowed in default public zone
First attempt used two rich-rules in the public zone (accept 9000 from node2, reject 9000 from all); functional test showed node2 was also incorrectly blocked

Diagnosed via iptables -S IN_public that firewalld's chain always jumps to the deny chain before the allow chain, so a blanket reject in the same zone blocks everyone including the intended allow source regardless of add order
Tried firewalld rich-rule priority attribute to reorder evaluation; rejected as unsupported (INVALID_RULE: bad attribute 'priority') on this RHEL7 firewalld version

Redesigned using a dedicated source-based zone 'node2-9000' (source=10.100.190.11/32, services=ssh, ports=9000/tcp) while the public zone keeps ssh and adds a reject rich-rule for 9000/tcp for all other sources; applied with --permanent and --reload
Verified via iptables that node2's traffic is routed via INPUT_ZONES_SOURCE into IN_node2-9000 (accept happens before any deny check), while all other traffic remains in the public zone's reject path
Functionally verified with a temporary listener on 9000: node2 gets HTTP 200 and SSH works; node3 gets connection refused on 9000 but SSH still works
Confirmed persistence by reading /etc/firewalld/zones/node2-9000.xml and public.xml on disk, matching the active runtime config
Captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime/firewalld-state baselines on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via 'sudo -n reboot', polled until SSH/exec access returned, confirmed changed boot_id and that firewalld came back active with all zones/rules intact
Restarted node2, polled until back, confirmed changed boot_id, sshd active, and cross-node connectivity to node1 preserved
Restarted node3, polled until back, confirmed changed boot_id, sshd active, and SSH reachability to node1 preserved
Ran a final end-to-end functional re-check after all three reboots: node2 reaches 9000 (200), node3 is refused on 9000, SSH open from both; cleaned up the temporary test listener on node1

evidence.requirement: SSH allowed from any address on node1
evidence.summary: public zone has ssh service enabled with no source restriction; verified reachable from both node2 and node3
dedicated zone 'node2-9000' scoped to source 10.100.190.11/32 opens port 9000/tcp; curl from node2 to node1:9000 returns http_code=200 both before and after all node restarts

evidence.requirement: TCP/9000 rejected from node3 and everywhere else
evidence.summary: public zone rich-rule rejects tcp/9000 for all non-node2-9000-zone sources; curl from node3 to node1:9000 fails with connection refused (rc=7) both before and after all node restarts
permanent XML files in /etc/firewalld/zones/ hold the config; after node1's own reboot, firewalld came back active with the same zones, ports, services, and rich rules

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence (baseline, restart ack, changed boot id, recovered state)
evidence.summary: baseline boot_id 738d0aac...; reboot command acknowledged via dropped connection; post-reboot probe succeeded; boot_id changed to d5df004c... with firewalld active and rules intact
baseline boot_id fe422859...; reboot acknowledged; probe succeeded after downtime; boot_id changed to 76d13a34... with sshd active and cross-node SSH to node1 confirmed
baseline boot_id 2fc81aed...; reboot acknowledged; probe succeeded after downtime; boot_id changed to 5f2e6b13... with sshd active and SSH to node1 confirmed reachable
